title: Greeting an Elder in Ijebu Ode
summary: Tunde visits his grandmother Mama Iyabo in Ijebu Ode, prostrating respectfully and discussing breakfast prepared with fresh yam and courtyard fowl.
culturalNote: In Yoruba culture, a young man prostrates (dọ̀bálẹ̀) and a young woman kneels (kúnlẹ̀) when greeting an elder. Using the honorific plural pronoun 'ẹ' is mandatory when addressing anyone older.

script.text: Ẹ kú àárọ̀, Màmá. Mo dọ̀bálẹ̀.
script.translation: Good morning, Grandmother. I prostrate in respect.

script.text: Àárọ̀ire o, ọmọ mi. Dìde, ẹ káàbọ̀ sílé.
script.translation: A good morning to you, my child. Rise, welcome home.

script.text: Ṣé àlàáfíà ni gbogbo ilé wà, Màmá?
script.translation: Is the whole household in good health, Grandmother?

script.text: Aúpẹ́ o. Ọkọ mi ti lọ sí oko ní àárọ̀ yìí.
script.translation: We give thanks. My husband went to the farm this morning.

script.text: Ṣé ọkọ̀ Baba ṣì ń ṣiṣẹ́ dáadáa?
script.translation: Is Grandfather's vehicle still working well?

script.text: Bẹ́ẹ̀ni, ó gbé usu àti ẹdiyẹ wá láti oko àná.
script.translation: Yes, he brought yam and fowl from the farm yesterday.

script.text: Inú mi dùn! Mo fẹ́ràn usu jíjẹ púpọ̀.
script.translation: I am delighted! I love eating yam very much.

script.text: Gba omi tútù kọ́kọ́, oúnjẹ tietan níbi ìdáná.
script.translation: Take cool water first, the food is ready in the kitchen.

title: Morning Compound Greeting in Ado-Ekiti
summary: Bisi greets her uncle Baba Ade in an Ado-Ekiti family compound and helps prepare morning water and pounded yam.
culturalNote: Ekiti speakers prize warm morning inquiries after every member of the compound before discussing any errand or request.

script.text: Ẹ kú àárọ̀, Bàbá. Mo kúnlẹ̀ o.
script.translation: Good morning, Father. I kneel in greeting.

script.text: Ọmọ rere, dìde. Ṣé o jíire lónìí?
script.translation: Good child, rise. Did you wake well today?

script.text: Mo jíire, Bàbá. Mo mú omi wá fún yín.
script.translation: I woke well, Father. I brought water for you.

script.text: Ọlọ́run á bùkún ọ. Níbo ni ìyá rẹ wà?
script.translation: May God bless you. Where is your mother?

script.text: Ìyá wà nínú ilé, wọ́n ń se iyán.
script.translation: Mother is inside the house, she is preparing pounded yam.

script.text: Iyán àti ọbẹ̀ ewédú dára ní àárọ̀.
script.translation: Pounded yam and ewedu soup are wonderful in the morning.

script.text: Mo ti fọ abọ́ àti ọwọ́ mi.
script.translation: I have washed the bowls and my hands.

script.text: Ó dára, pe àwọn àbúrò rẹ kí a jọ jẹun.
script.translation: Very good, call your younger siblings so we eat together.

title: Preparing Festival Supper in Ondo Town
summary: Ayo helps Auntie Funke sort yams and seasoning in Ondo Town while learning local Ondo words.
culturalNote: In Ondo homes, helping elders in the courtyard kitchen is a traditional way younger relatives learn proverbs and regional vocabulary.

script.text: Ẹ kú iṣẹ́ o, Àńtí Fúnkẹ́.
script.translation: Well done with your work, Auntie Funke.

script.text: Oo, Ayọ̀. Wa bá mi gbé usu yẹn.
script.translation: Thank you, Ayo. Come help me carry that yam.

script.text: Usu náà tóbi gan-an! Láti ọjà ni?
script.translation: That yam is very big! Is it from the market?

script.text: Rárá, láti oko wa ni. Mú iyọ̀ àti ata wá.
script.translation: No, it is from our farm. Bring the salt and pepper.

script.text: Èyí ni iyọ̀, èyí sì ni ata pupa.
script.translation: Here is the salt, and here is the red pepper.

script.text: Ẹdiyẹ náà ti jóná lórí iná.
script.translation: The chicken is cooked on the fire.

script.text: oorùn ọbẹ̀ náà dùn púpọ̀.
script.translation: The aroma of the soup is very pleasant.

script.text: Jókòó kí o tọ́ ọbẹ̀ náà wò.
script.translation: Sit down and taste the soup.

title: Visiting Nne in Owerri
summary: Adaeze arrives from London with her children to greet her mother Nne Ngozi in Owerri, sharing kola nut and palm wine blessings.
culturalNote: In Igboland, welcoming a guest begins with presenting kola nut (ọ́jị̀). The proverb 'Onye wetara ọjị wetara ndụ' means 'Whoever brings kola brings life.'

script.text: Nnọọ, Nné m! Anyị erutela n'ụ́lọ̀.
script.translation: Hello, my Mother! We have arrived home.

script.text: Nnọọ, nwa m ọ́ma! Ụ́mụ̀ m, bịanụ.
script.translation: Welcome, my good child! My grandchildren, come closer.

script.text: Ụ́tụ́tụ́ ọ́ma, Nné. Kedu ka ị mere?
script.translation: Good morning, Mother. How are you doing?

script.text: Ọ́ dị̀ mma. Weta mmírí ka ha ṅụọ.
script.translation: It is well. Bring water so they can drink.

script.text: Nné, lee ọ́jị̀ anyị ji bịa.
script.translation: Mother, behold the kola nut we brought.

script.text: Onye wetara ọ́jị̀ wetara ndụ̀. Chukwu gozie unu.
script.translation: Whoever brings kola brings life. May God bless you all.

script.text: Isee! Ụ́mụ̀aka chọrọ ịmụ olu Owerri.
script.translation: Amen! The children want to learn the Owerri dialect.

script.text: Obi dị m ụtọ. Anyị ga-eri jí na ofe Owerri taa.
script.translation: My heart is glad. We will eat yam and Owerri soup today.

title: Buying Yams at Ose Okwodu Market in Onitsha
summary: Chidi negotiates politely with Mama Ifeoma for Niger-grown yams and fresh palm oil in Onitsha.
culturalNote: In Onitsha markets, respectful address ('Mama', 'Nwanne m') before asking the price sets a friendly tone for bargaining.

speakers.role: Yam trader at Ose Okwodu Market

script.text: Nnọọ, Màmá. Kedu ego ole jí a bụ?
script.translation: Hello, Mama. How much money is this yam?

script.text: Nwanne m, jí a mara mma. Ọ́ bụ̀ puku naira abụọ.
script.translation: My sibling, this yam is fine. It is two thousand naira.

script.text: Biko, belata ego ntakịrị. Achọrọ m ịzụ anọ.
script.translation: Please, reduce the price a little. I want to buy four.

script.text: Ngwanụ, kwụọ puku isii maka anọ ahụ.
script.translation: All right, pay six thousand for those four.

script.text: Ị nwere mmanụ nri ọhụrụ taa?
script.translation: Do you have fresh palm oil today?

script.text: Ee, mmanụ a si n'obodo bịa n'ụtụtụ a.
script.translation: Yes, this palm oil came from the village this morning.

script.text: Tinye otu karama. Lee ego gị.
script.translation: Add one bottle. Here is your money.

script.text: Daalụ rinne! Laa n'udo.
script.translation: Thank you very much! Go home in peace.

title: Welcoming Relatives in an Ikwerre Compound
summary: Elder Wobo welcomes his niece Chinyere and the community children in Port Harcourt, highlighting Ikwerre kinship terms.
culturalNote: In Ikwerre (Port Harcourt region), 'rụmụ' corresponds to Standard Igbo 'ụmụ' (children or descendants), visible in place names such as Rumuola and Rumuokoro.

script.text: M̀gbọ́ ọ́ma, Nnà anyị.
script.translation: Good day, our Father.

script.text: Nnọọ, Chinyere. Kedu maka rụmụ gị?
script.translation: Welcome, Chinyere. How are your children?

script.text: Rụmụ dị mma, ha nọ n'èzí na-egwu egwu.
script.translation: The children are fine, they are outside playing.

script.text: Kpọọ rụmụ ahụ ka ha bịa nata ngọzi.
script.translation: Call those children so they come receive a blessing.

script.text: Anyị wetara azụ̀ ọhụrụ si n'osimiri.
script.translation: We brought fresh fish from the river.

script.text: Ọ́ dị̀ mma! Azụ̀ na jí ga-atọ ụtọ.
script.translation: That is wonderful! Fish and yam will be delicious.

script.text: Ka m nyere Nné aka n'usekwu.
script.translation: Let me help Mother in the kitchen.

script.text: Chukwu debe unu niile.
script.translation: May God preserve you all.

title: Bargaining for Indigo Cloth at Kurmi Market in Kano
summary: Amina visits Mallam Musa's stall in Kano's historic Kurmi Market, exchanging morning greetings before negotiating for hand-dyed fabric.
culturalNote: In Kano Hausa culture, jumping straight to price without asking after health, family, and the morning ('Ina kwana?') is considered hurried. Patience earns respect and a fair price.

script.text: Sannu da aiki, Mallam Musa. Ina kwana?
script.translation: Greetings at your work, Mallam Musa. How did you sleep?

script.text: Lafiya lau, Hajiya Amina. Yaya gida da iyali?
script.translation: In good health, Hajiya Amina. How are the home and family?

script.text: Alhamdulillahi, kowa lafiya. Nawa ne wannan zannuwa?
script.translation: Praise be to God, everyone is well. How much is this wrapper cloth?

script.text: Wannan rini na Kofar Mata ne. Dubu takwas ne.
script.translation: This is indigo-dyed cloth from Kofar Mata. It is eight thousand naira.

script.text: Yi hakuri, Mallam. Rage mana kadan, zan sayi biyu.
script.translation: Have patience, Mallam. Reduce it a little for us, I will buy two.

script.text: Toh, saboda ke, kawo dubu sha hudu duka biyun.
script.translation: All right, because of you, bring fourteen thousand for both.

script.text: Nagode sosai. Ga kudin nan.
script.translation: Thank you very much. Here is the money.

script.text: Allah ya sa albarka. Sai anjima!
script.translation: May God put blessing in it. See you later!

title: Navigating a Danfo from Yaba to Obalende
summary: Emeka boards a yellow Lagos danfo bus at Yaba, checking fare and change with the conductor before calling his stop.
culturalNote: In Lagos transit, telling the conductor early if you hold a large note ('I hold thousand naira') and calling your stop clearly ('Owa o!') keeps the ride smooth for everyone.

script.text: Obalende, CMS! Enter with your change o!
script.translation: Obalende, CMS! Board with your exact fare!

script.text: How far, Broda. How much be Obalende now?
script.translation: Hello, Brother. How much is the fare to Obalende now?

script.text: Na five hundred naira. No wahala, enter sharp-sharp.
script.translation: It is five hundred naira. No problem, hop in quickly.

script.text: Abeg, na one thousand naira I hold. You get change?
script.translation: Please, I have a one-thousand-naira note. Do you have change?

script.text: I dey kampe, change dey. Sit down for back seat.
script.translation: I am all set, there is change. Sit in the back row.

script.text: Driver sabi road well-well, we don pass Third Mainland.
script.translation: The driver knows the route well, we have already passed Third Mainland Bridge.

script.text: Oya, collect your five hundred balance. Who dey drop for junction?
script.translation: Here, take your five hundred change. Who is alighting at the junction?

script.text: Owa o! Driver, abeg drop me for Obalende under bridge.
script.translation: Stop here please! Driver, kindly let me off at Obalende under the bridge.
